Thanks Olga — great session. Quick answers inline and attaching our security requirements bundle (PDF):

1) Data types: Correct. Transaction metadata is non-PII. Payment descriptors and support transcripts can contain PII. For the POC we can scope transcripts to redacted samples, but we need a path to handle real transcripts in production.

2) Retention: Our baseline policy is 90 days for logs, 365 days for customer support transcripts unless specifically shortened by contract. We can negotiate 30/90/365 depending on classification.

3) Telemetry: We use Datadog for metrics and Segment (analytics) for behavioral events. For initial POC we prefer no raw traffic or PII to be sent to Segment. Datadog metrics are fine if they are aggregated and do not include PII. If Redwood requires any forwarding to a telemetry vendor, we need: (a) list of fields forwarded, (b) subprocessor contract terms, and (c) confirmation that forwarded payloads are pseudonymized.

4) Subprocessors/DPA: attaching our standard security questionnaire (AtlasPay_Security_Reqs.pdf). We typically require an explicit subprocessor list for anything that touches customer data.

Attached: AtlasPay_Security_Reqs.pdf (stub)

We can do 10/08 for a follow-up. Prefer 10:00am PT.

Hi Sarah / Rajiv — thanks for the quick turnaround and the questionnaire. I’m Marcus (Head of Applied ML Ops at Redwood); copying Olga and Laura for continuity. Below is a concise technical note and proposed MAP for the POC.

Technical note (summary):
- Dataflow & PII handling: By default Redwood treats customer content as segregated, and we do not forward raw customer content to third-party analytics vendors. For the POC we recommend:
  * Ingress: all traffic to Redwood is TLS-encrypted and optionally routed into a customer-specific VPC when on Redwood Private.
  * Pre-processing: any fields explicitly marked as PII (email, SSN, full payment details) are redacted at the client or via an ingress scrubber before persisting or being sent to model context. For support transcripts we can apply a configurable PII scrub pipeline (we supply a recommended ruleset).
  * Telemetry exporter policy: metrics -> Datadog only in aggregated form (counts, latencies, error-rates). No event-level payloads that contain PII will be forwarded. For Segment/behavioral vendors: we will not forward event data that contains identifiers unless AtlasPay signs a subprocessor addendum (DocuSign link below) and defines an allowlist of fields.

- Retention defaults & contract controls:
  * Logs/metrics: default 90 days retention for non-content logs; aggregated metrics retained per AtlasPay preference.
  * Model contexts / KV cache: default 7 days for POC; configurable up to 365 days in contract with explicit opt-in.
  * Transcripts / customer content: default 30 days for POC redacted samples; production default will follow contract (90/365 options).

- Subprocessors & what they touch:
  * Cloud provider: AWS (us-west-2) — infrastructure only, does not access decrypted customer content without our KMS keys.
  * Telemetry: Datadog — metrics only (aggregated).
  * Optional analytics (Segment) — would require a subprocessor agreement and explicit allowlist before any data is shared.

Proposed MAP (POC milestones):
1) Week 0: Exchange signed DPA + subprocessor list; agree retention windows for POC (target: 90-day logs, 7-day model context).
2) Week 1: Deploy POC in a dedicated project; send redacted transcript samples and validation harness.
3) Week 2–3: Run validation, confirm telemetry exports are aggregated and produce a short audit log showing no PII forwarded.

Security attachments I’ll provide: redwood-dataflow-diagram.png (shows ingress, scrubber, model runtime, optional telemetry exporter) and short subprocessor list.

Quick answers to Sarah’s specific asks:
- Field list for telemetry: we will only forward counts, latency histograms, error codes, and anonymized request size buckets. No user identifiers, IP addresses, or transcript text.
- Pseudonymization: we can implement hashing for identifiers for aggregated analysis, but hashing alone is not a substitute for agreeing DPA/subprocessor terms for production flows.
- Region options: we can run POC in us-west-2; EU residency is available on Dedicated/Private deployments and we can propose an EU-only hosting plan if required for production.

If that looks good I’ll attach the diagram and a one-page subprocessor list as discussed. Olga — happy for you to send this back to Sarah with the attachments and the proposed 10/08 10:00am PT meeting.
